summary_en: ASUA Inc. will acquire all issued shares of JCL Inc., a Japanese language school with approximately 600 students, for 1,260 million yen, making it a wholly owned subsidiary. The acquisition is part of ASUA's strategy to build a Global HR business combining education, staffing, and talent retention services for foreign workers.
title_en: Notice Regarding Acquisition of Shares in JCL Inc. (Making it a Wholly Owned Subsidiary)
translation_en_brief:
On November 13, 2026, ASUA Inc. resolved to acquire all issued shares of JCL Inc., a Japanese language education institution, and make it a wholly owned subsidiary. JCL operates a Japanese language school in Kyoto with approximately 600 enrolled students and holds accreditation from the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology. The school has demonstrated stable educational operations with growing profitability over the past three years: operating profit increased from 94.2 million yen in the fiscal year ended July 2024 to 201.9 million yen in the fiscal year ended July 2026.

ASUA is positioning this acquisition not merely as the purchase of a language school, but as the acquisition of a high-barrier business foundation in Japanese language education combined with the creation of a career support platform for foreign workers. The total acquisition cost is approximately 1,290 million yen, including 1,260 million yen for share acquisition and approximately 30 million yen in advisory fees. ASUA intends to enter the personnel placement business concurrently with this acquisition.

The company aims to establish an integrated business model providing education, staffing referral, and retention support services to match foreign workers with Japanese employers. This new "Global HR business" is positioned as a growth pillar to expand ASUA's business portfolio through value-creation oriented M&A. The existing management team, with representative directors Eiyoyo Yoshinaga and Kenji Kimura, will continue to participate in management while pursuing growth through coordination with the ASUA group. Current educational policies and operational systems will be maintained.
